edit.description: `assemble_lock_family`'s local-locus pre-pass (:1121) keeps each local kind's resolved units beside the rows it derives from them; `read_dial` (:1059) builds the `Dial` off the `dial` entry it finds there rather than calling `kind_features` — and through it `resolve_kind_units` — a second time on the same kind, same discovery, same committed declarations, same cache. The overlaid `dial` is always `Commitment::Local` (`overlay_builtin_kind` overlays governs, templates and content only, never commitment), so the entry is always present and no re-resolving fallback is needed. The pre-pass's doc gains the sentence that closes this class: the judging pass's later read of the same kind is a second read, not a removable third, because it ranges over the *assembled* family whose local rows this pass produces.

`resolve_kind_units_runs_once_per_kind_not_twice` (:806): `expected` (:878) drops its trailing `+ 1` dial term, and the comment (:862-:872) and assertion message stop naming the captured third resolution — the shipped count is every built-in, plus the locked `custom-kind`, plus one pre-pass per local-locus kind.

Reached only if the retained units ride a new `LockFamily` field: the destructure at :167 is deliberately `..`-free, so a new field lands here as a compile error rather than a silent drop. No verdict changes at this site.

summary: Fold `read_dial`'s resolution of the `dial` kind onto the local-locus pre-pass that already resolved it — one dial read per run, and the count pin loses its `dial` term.

per.section: Cost scale is hoisted, and pinned by count

tests.asserts: `resolve_kind_units_runs_once_per_kind_not_twice` pins `builtins.len() + 1 + locals` — 18 for its fixture, down from 19 — so a re-added dial resolution fails hard
the dial suite is unchanged and green, `a_lock_relocating_the_dial_kind_governs_is_honored` in particular: the dial is still read at the locus the lock's overlay relocated it to

acceptance: cargo test green with the count pin asserting the dial term gone (18 for its fixture, 19 before), and tests/it/dial_kind.rs green untouched. The commit body names the surviving second read of a local kind and why the assembled family it reads makes it load-bearing.
notes: Drains .flume/refactor/build-dial-is-resolved-three-times-per-run.md. Re-verified at HEAD: the pin passes at 19 = 15 built-ins + 1 custom + 2 local pre-passes + 1 dial. The capture's third read is not folded — the judging pass reads the assembled family (a local layout kind's satisfies and nested rows, derived by the pre-pass itself), so it cannot reuse a pre-pass unit. 19 to 18, never 19 to 17. scoped at ea365018
